title: Compatibility Fabric & Deployment Spiral for Private Upgrades
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: Create a composable "compatibility fabric" and deployment-spiral workflow that enables zero-downtime, orchestrated migrations for Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) customers across LTS channels. This ticket focuses on the upgrade runner, routing/rollout gates, compatibility probes, and migration telemetry required to safely advance fleets through staged channels (canary -> cohort -> general).

Scope:
- Define a compatibility fabric abstraction that encapsulates compatibility checks for API surface, storage schema, plugin contracts, and third-party integrations.
- Implement a Deployment Spiral controller: an orchestrator that moves cohorts through phases (preflight -> canary -> staggered cohorts -> full) with gated rollback and checkpointing.
- Add version-aware rollout policies that understand LTS channels and allow pinning/rollback by channel.
- Integrate transactional migration runner for database/schema changes including idempotent steps and dry-run mode.
- Add migration telemetry and regression detection hooks to Console (per-cohort dashboards and early-warning signals).
- Provide operator-facing CLIs and web-console views for pause/resume, force-transition, and emergency-rollback.

Non-goals: Automated schema rewriting of customer data (we provide runners and safety hooks; customer-specific transforms run in their environment).

Rationale: Existing Private upgrade tooling is heavy on one-off playbooks and ad-hoc steps. Customers with strict SLAs need deterministic, auditable upgrades across hybrid topologies. The compatibility fabric concept centralizes checks so the Deployment Spiral can make binary progress decisions rather than ad-hoc heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility fabric API defined and documented in Confluence with interfaces for: API sanity probes, schema validators, binary compatibility checks, and plugin contract validators.
Deployment Spiral controller implemented as a k8s operator + CLI (test harness) with phase transitions and checkpointing persisted to the upgrade state store.
Two-phase canary flow demonstrated: a single-node canary + 3 staggered cohorts in a dry-run on staging with at least one simulated rollback.
Transactional migration runner supports: preflight dry-run, idempotent step execution, pause/resume, and automatic rollback on failure of a defined step.
Console telemetry surface added: per-cohort latency/cost/err-rate charts and automated alerting rules for regressions (configurable thresholds).
Runbook and operator docs published with GitHub PR linking install instructions and troubleshooting steps.

rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Preflight: Run compatibility fabric checks across API surface and plugin contracts in target environment. Block if any high-severity check fails.
Phase 1 - Canary: Deploy to one canary node/cohort with traffic mirroring. Monitor latency, error-rate, and KV cache hit patterns for 6 hours (configurable).
Phase 2 - Staggered cohorts: Move to 3 cohorts (10% each) with 15-minute stabilization windows and automated rollback triggers if thresholds breached.
Phase 3 - General: Full rollout across remaining cohorts with long-term monitoring and auto-revert policy available for 72 hours post-upgrade.
Emergency: Operator may 'quarantine' cohorts (pause ingress) and initiate an orchestrated rollback using the migration runner's checkpointed snapshot.
migration_steps: Step A - Preflight dry-run: Validate migrations against a cloned schema (no write). Produce a compatibility report.
Step B - Backup checkpoint: Snapshot critical metadata and write encrypted checkpoint to configured state store.
Step C - Apply non-destructive schema changes (idempotent): run migration runner in single-node mode with step-level retries.
Step D - Schema activation gating: Flip feature flags / runtime gates after cohort stabilization window.
Step E - Data backfill (if required): Run background idempotent backfills with coordination tokens to avoid double writes.
Step F - Finalize: Mark upgrade completed and persist final manifest for audit and possible rollback window.
telemetry_requirements: Per-cohort histograms for p95/p99 latency, token-per-request distribution, and request error-class breakdown.
Migration-runner events: step_started, step_completed, step_failed, rollback_started, rollback_completed (structured logs with trace IDs).
Drift detection probes comparing preflight vs postflight API responses for a canonical prompt set; produce similarity scores and raise alerts if below threshold.
Retention: keep upgrade telemetry for 90 days and attach to customer audit bundle on-demand.
